pinyin: shí gè shǒu zhǐ yǒu cháng duǎn
literal: ten · fingers · have · long · short
natural: The ten fingers are not all the same length

meaning.en: People differ in ability and circumstance, so equality of outcome should not be expected.
meaning.zh: 人与人各有差异，不可能完全一样，不必强求一律。

equivalents: All fingers are not alike
There are all sorts in the world

examples.zh: 十个手指有长短，同一个班的学生成绩不可能都一样。
examples.en: The ten fingers are not all the same length, and the pupils in one class can't all get the same marks.

examples.zh: 十个手指有长短，别拿孩子跟别人比。
examples.en: No two fingers are alike, so don't compare your child with other people's.

usage.en: Often used to ask for tolerance of differences between children or colleagues.
usage.zh: 常用于劝人容忍子女、同事之间的差异。

synonyms: 一母生九子，九子各不同

text: 一母生九子，九子各不同
pinyin: yī mǔ shēng jiǔ zǐ, jiǔ zǐ gè bù tóng
literal: one · mother · bear · nine · sons, nine · sons · each · not · alike
natural: One mother has nine sons, and all nine differ

meaning.en: Even children of the same parents have different characters and fates.
meaning.zh: 同一个母亲生的孩子，性格和命运也各不相同。

equivalents: No two children are alike
Children of the same parents can be very different

examples.zh: 一母生九子，九子各不同，兄弟俩的脾气完全不一样。
examples.en: One mother bears nine sons and all nine differ; the two brothers have completely different temperaments.

examples.zh: 一母生九子，九子各不同，不能要求每个孩子都一样优秀。
examples.en: Children of one mother are all different; you can't expect every child to be equally outstanding.

usage.en: Often said when comparing siblings. The number nine just means 'many'.
usage.zh: 常用于谈论兄弟姐妹的差异；“九”泛指多。

pinyin: hǔ dú bù shí zǐ
literal: tiger · fierce · not · eat · cubs
natural: Even a fierce tiger doesn't eat its young

meaning.en: Even the cruellest creatures care for their own children, so it is monstrous for a parent to harm a child.
meaning.zh: 再凶残的老虎也不吃自己的孩子，用来说明父母不会伤害亲生子女。

equivalents: Even a tiger loves its cubs
Even beasts love their young

examples.zh: 虎毒不食子，他怎么能这样对待自己的孩子？
examples.en: Even tigers don't eat their young; how could he treat his own child this way?

examples.zh: 俗话说虎毒不食子，可这对父母竟然把孩子遗弃了。
examples.en: As the saying goes, even tigers don't eat their young, yet these parents abandoned their child.

usage.en: Used to condemn parents who harm children; also to express confidence that parents will protect their children.
usage.zh: 多用于谴责虐待子女的父母，也可表示相信父母不会害孩子。

pinyin: lǎo hǔ pì gu mō bù dé
literal: tiger · bottom · touch · cannot
natural: You must not touch a tiger's backside

meaning.en: Some powerful or touchy people cannot be provoked or criticised.
meaning.zh: 有些人或事不能触碰，一碰就会招来麻烦。

equivalents: Let sleeping dogs lie
Don't beard the lion in his den

examples.zh: 他是公司老板的亲戚，老虎屁股摸不得，谁也不敢批评。
examples.en: He is related to the boss, and nobody dares to criticise a man who can't be touched.

examples.zh: 老虎屁股摸不得，别去惹那个脾气大的人。
examples.en: You can't touch a tiger's backside, so don't provoke that bad-tempered person.

usage.en: A casual warning about touchy people, taboo topics or powerful figures.
usage.zh: 口头提醒不要触碰脾气大、惹不起的人或敏感话题。

text: 山中无老虎，猴子称大王
pinyin: shān zhōng wú lǎo hǔ, hóu zi chēng dà wáng
variants: 山中无老虎，猴子称霸王
literal: mountain · in · no · tiger, monkey · call · oneself · great · king
natural: With no tiger in the mountain, the monkey calls himself king

meaning.en: When no capable person is around, a mediocre one can play the boss.
meaning.zh: 没有真正有本事的人在场，平庸的人就充当首领。

equivalents: In the kingdom of the blind, the one-eyed man is king
A big fish in a small pond

examples.zh: 山中无老虎，猴子称大王，他在这个小公司里最能干。
examples.en: With no tiger around, the monkey becomes king; he's the most capable in this little company.

examples.zh: 队长请假了，山中无老虎，猴子称大王，他便指挥起大家来。
examples.en: The captain was on leave, and with the tiger away the monkey played king and began ordering everyone about.

usage.en: Scornful when aimed at someone; can be self-mocking when said of oneself. Often shortened to 山中无老虎.
usage.zh: 对他人含讥讽，对自己则是自嘲；常简作“山中无老虎”。

synonyms: 蜀中无大将，廖化作先锋

pinyin: guān dà yī jí yā sǐ rén
literal: official · bigger · one · rank · crush · dead · people
natural: One rank higher can crush you to death

meaning.en: Even a slightly higher rank gives great power over subordinates, who cannot argue back.
meaning.zh: 哪怕只高一级，也能让下级无法反抗。

equivalents: Rank has its privileges
The boss is always right

examples.zh: 官大一级压死人，我只好听领导的。
examples.en: One rank higher can crush you, so I had to do what my boss said.

examples.zh: 在这种单位里，官大一级压死人，没人敢提意见。
examples.en: In an organisation like this, rank means everything and nobody dares to complain.

usage.en: Complaining about hierarchy and bureaucracy; always humorous or resentful.
usage.zh: 多用来抱怨等级森严的官场或职场，带怨气或调侃。

pinyin: xiàn guān bù rú xiàn guǎn
literal: county · magistrate · not as good as · actual · manager
natural: The county magistrate counts for less than the one in charge

meaning.en: The person who directly controls a matter matters more than a higher official with no immediate authority.
meaning.zh: 直接管事的人比级别更高却不直接管的人更有实权。

equivalents: The man on the spot matters more than the one far away
He who pays the piper calls the tune

examples.zh: 县官不如现管，你得罪了直属领导，局长也帮不了你。
examples.en: The one directly in charge matters more than the magistrate; you've offended your direct boss and even the director can't help you.

examples.zh: 县官不如现管，办这件事还得找科长。
examples.en: The person who actually handles it has the real power, so you must go to the section chief.

usage.en: Often said when one needs to please the actual decision-maker. 现 here means 'at present, on the spot'.
usage.zh: 常用于要讨好直接管事的人的场合；“现”意为当下、在场。

pinyin: guó yǒu guó fǎ, jiā yǒu jiā guī
literal: country · has · country · law, family · has · family · rules
natural: Every country has its laws and every family its rules

meaning.en: Every community has rules that must be followed.
meaning.zh: 任何集体都有规矩，大家必须遵守。

equivalents: When in Rome, do as the Romans do
Rules are rules

examples.zh: 国有国法，家有家规，进了公司就得守公司的规矩。
examples.en: Every country has its laws and every family its rules; once you join a company, you must abide by its rules.

examples.zh: 国有国法，家有家规，孩子犯了错也要受罚。
examples.en: A country has laws and a family has rules, so a child who does wrong must also face a penalty.

usage.en: Used to demand compliance; the family clause makes it sound domestic and firm.
usage.zh: 用来要求遵守规矩，后半句带家常而坚定的语气。

pinyin: wáng zǐ fàn fǎ, yǔ shù mín tóng zuì
literal: prince · break · law, with · commoner · same · guilt
natural: If a prince breaks the law, he is as guilty as a commoner

meaning.en: Everyone is equal before the law, whatever their rank.
meaning.zh: 法律面前人人平等，不论地位高低。

equivalents: No one is above the law
The law is no respecter of persons

examples.zh: 王子犯法，与庶民同罪，不管他是谁都要依法处理。
examples.en: Everyone is equal before the law, so he will be dealt with according to law whoever he is.

examples.zh: 王子犯法，与庶民同罪，这是法治社会的基本原则。
examples.en: A prince guilty of an offence is punished like a commoner; this is a basic principle of a society ruled by law.

usage.en: Used in discussions of the rule of law, anti-corruption and fairness; commonly recited in full.
usage.zh: 多用于谈法治、反腐和公平，常整句引用。

pinyin: chī kuī shì fú
literal: eat · loss · is · blessing
natural: Taking a loss is a blessing

meaning.en: Accepting a small loss can bring greater benefit and peace of mind in the long run.
meaning.zh: 肯吃亏的人往往会得到更长远的好处和心安。

equivalents: Better a small loss than a great quarrel
Loss may be gain in disguise

examples.zh: 吃亏是福，别跟他计较那点钱。
examples.en: Taking a loss is a blessing; don't quarrel with him over that bit of money.

examples.zh: 老人常说吃亏是福，做人不要太斤斤计较。
examples.en: The old folks say that a loss can be a blessing, and that you shouldn't be too calculating.

usage.en: Often attributed to Zheng Banqiao's calligraphy 难得糊涂，吃亏是福. A mix of wisdom and consolation; sometimes criticised as encouraging people to be taken advantage of.
usage.zh: 常与郑板桥“难得糊涂，吃亏是福”并提；既是处世智慧，也是自我安慰，有时被批评为纵容吃亏。

pinyin: chī shuǐ bù wàng wā jǐng rén
literal: drink · water · not · forget · dig · well · person
natural: When drinking water, remember who dug the well

meaning.en: Remember and be grateful to those who made your present happiness possible.
meaning.zh: 享受成果时不要忘记创造条件的人，要知恩感恩。

equivalents: Don't bite the hand that feeds you
Remember the bridge that carried you over

examples.zh: 吃水不忘挖井人，我们不会忘记老师的教导。
examples.en: When drinking the water, remember who dug the well; we won't forget our teacher's guidance.

examples.zh: 吃水不忘挖井人，他功成名就后捐款建了学校。
examples.en: Mindful of whoever dug the well, he donated money to build a school after he became successful.

usage.en: Became a political slogan in the 1930s (Mao's village of Shaping). Frequently used in speeches about gratitude. Also 吃水不忘掘井人.
usage.zh: 三十年代与毛泽东沙洲坝挖井的故事相关，常用于感恩类讲话；也作“吃水不忘掘井人”。

pinyin: chī zhe wǎn lǐ, kàn zhe guō lǐ
literal: eat · -ing · bowl · in, look · -ing · pot · in
natural: Eating from the bowl while eyeing the pot

meaning.en: Never being satisfied with what you have; always looking for something more or someone else.
meaning.zh: 不满足于已有的，还惦记着别的。

equivalents: Having your cake and eating it
Grass is always greener on the other side
The eye is bigger than the belly

examples.zh: 你吃着碗里，看着锅里，到头来什么都得不到。
examples.en: You eat what's in the bowl while eyeing the pot, and in the end you'll get nothing.

examples.zh: 他有了女朋友还想着别人，真是吃着碗里，看着锅里。
examples.en: He has a girlfriend but is thinking of others; he's never satisfied.

usage.en: A criticism of greed or unfaithfulness; often said of romantic infidelity. Variant: 吃着碗里，瞧着锅里.
usage.zh: 批评贪心或不专一，常用于感情不忠；也说“吃着碗里，瞧着锅里”。

pinyin: chī bú dào pú táo shuō pú táo suān
literal: eat · cannot · reach · grape · say · grape · sour
natural: Unable to get the grapes, he says they are sour

meaning.en: To belittle what you cannot have, in order to console yourself.
meaning.zh: 得不到的东西，就说它不好，以此安慰自己。

equivalents: Sour grapes

examples.zh: 他没被录取就说那所学校不好，真是吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸。
examples.en: He said the school was no good because he wasn't admitted; that's sour grapes.

examples.zh: 别吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸，承认别人比你强吧。
examples.en: Don't say the grapes are sour just because you can't reach them; admit that others are better.

usage.en: A direct counterpart of the Aesop fable 'sour grapes'; mildly mocking.
usage.zh: 与伊索寓言“酸葡萄”相应，略带嘲讽。

text: 饭后百步走，活到九十九
pinyin: fàn hòu bǎi bù zǒu, huó dào jiǔ shí jiǔ
literal: meal · after · hundred · steps · walk, live · to · ninety · nine
natural: Walk a hundred steps after a meal and live to ninety-nine

meaning.en: A short stroll after eating is good for your health and longevity.
meaning.zh: 饭后散散步有益健康，能长寿。

equivalents: An apple a day keeps the doctor away
Walk after dinner, live longer

examples.zh: 饭后百步走，活到九十九，咱们去公园走走吧。
examples.en: Walk a hundred steps after a meal and live to ninety-nine; let's take a stroll in the park.

examples.zh: 爷爷每天晚饭后都要散步，他说饭后百步走，活到九十九。
examples.en: Grandpa walks every evening after dinner, saying a stroll after meals brings long life.

usage.en: A common health rhyme for older people. Some believe it contradicts modern advice on resting after eating.
usage.zh: 常见的养生顺口溜，尤其是长辈常说。

pinyin: zǎo shuì zǎo qǐ shēn tǐ hǎo
literal: early · sleep · early · rise · body · good
natural: Early to bed and early to rise makes you healthy

meaning.en: Going to bed and getting up early is good for your health.
meaning.zh: 早睡早起有利于健康。

equivalents: Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise

examples.zh: 早睡早起身体好，别再熬夜了。
examples.en: Early to bed and early to rise makes for good health, so stop staying up late.

examples.zh: 妈妈总说早睡早起身体好。
examples.en: Mum always says that going to bed and getting up early keeps you healthy.

usage.en: A rhyme of everyday health advice, often said to children.
usage.zh: 日常养生口诀，常用于劝孩子。

pinyin: zǎo qǐ de niǎo er yǒu chóng chī
literal: early · rise · 's · bird · has · worm · eat
natural: The early bird gets the worm

meaning.en: Those who act early get the advantage.
meaning.zh: 行动早的人占先机，更容易有收获。

equivalents: The early bird catches the worm

examples.zh: 早起的鸟儿有虫吃，我们得赶早去排队。
examples.en: The early bird gets the worm, so we must go and queue early.

examples.zh: 早起的鸟儿有虫吃，抢先报名的人最有机会。
examples.en: The early bird gets the worm, and the first to register has the best chance.

usage.en: Matches the English proverb exactly (probably a calque). Casual; used in study and business advice.
usage.zh: 与英语谚语完全对应，大概是仿译；多用于学习和工作场合的劝告。

pinyin: jiǔ hòu tǔ zhēn yán
literal: wine · after · spit out · true · words
natural: After drinking, people speak the truth

meaning.en: People tend to reveal what they really think when drunk.
meaning.zh: 喝醉了的人容易说出心里话。

equivalents: In vino veritas
Drunken words are sober thoughts

examples.zh: 酒后吐真言，他喝多了才说出自己的苦衷。
examples.en: In wine there is truth; only after drinking too much did he reveal his troubles.

examples.zh: 酒后吐真言，昨晚他说的才是他的真实想法。
examples.en: What he said last night when drunk was his real opinion.

usage.en: Used about confessions and indiscretions after drinking. Sometimes also an excuse for rudeness.
usage.zh: 多指酒后表露真情或失言；有时也成了说话失礼的借口。

text: 开门七件事，柴米油盐酱醋茶
pinyin: kāi mén qī jiàn shì, chái mǐ yóu yán jiàng cù chá
literal: open · door · seven · things, firewood · rice · oil · salt · soy sauce · vinegar · tea
natural: Seven things when you open the door: firewood, rice, oil, salt, soy sauce, vinegar, tea

meaning.en: The seven basic daily necessities of a household; the ordinary needs of everyday life.
meaning.zh: 开门就要面对的七件家常开销，泛指日常生活的琐碎必需。

equivalents: The daily grind
Bread-and-butter issues

examples.zh: 开门七件事，柴米油盐酱醋茶，过日子就是这些琐事。
examples.en: The seven daily necessities are firewood, rice, oil, salt, soy sauce, vinegar and tea; that's the stuff of everyday life.

examples.zh: 成家以后才懂得开门七件事，柴米油盐酱醋茶有多不容易。
examples.en: Only after setting up a family did I understand how hard it is to provide life's seven necessities.

usage.en: Often used to evoke the details of housekeeping and cost of living. The second half alone is also said as a list.
usage.zh: 常用来形容过日子的琐碎和生活成本；后半句也单独作为常用并列说法。

text: 由俭入奢易，由奢入俭难
pinyin: yóu jiǎn rù shē yì, yóu shē rù jiǎn nán
literal: from · thrift · enter · extravagance · easy, from · extravagance · enter · thrift · hard
natural: Going from frugal to lavish is easy; going from lavish to frugal is hard

meaning.en: It is easy to get used to luxury but very hard to go back to a simple life.
meaning.zh: 过惯了奢侈的日子，再回到节俭很难。

equivalents: Easy come, easy go
Hard to go back to simple living once you are used to luxury

examples.zh: 由俭入奢易，由奢入俭难，所以平时要养成节约的习惯。
examples.en: It's easy to go from thrift to luxury but hard to go back, so we should form frugal habits.

examples.zh: 他花钱大手大脚，由俭入奢易，由奢入俭难，破产后很不适应。
examples.en: He spent freely; having grown used to luxury, he found bankruptcy hard to adjust to.

usage.en: Used as moral advice on frugality. Often attributed to Sima Guang's 《训俭示康》.
usage.zh: 用于劝人节俭；常认为出自司马光《训俭示康》。

pinyin: shǒu zhōng yǒu liáng, xīn zhōng bù huāng
literal: hand · in · have · grain, heart · in · not · panic
natural: With grain in hand, the heart is calm

meaning.en: Having a reserve of resources gives security and peace of mind.
meaning.zh: 手里有储备，心里就踏实。

equivalents: A penny saved is a penny earned
Prepare for a rainy day

examples.zh: 手中有粮，心中不慌，这些年他一直有存钱的习惯。
examples.en: With grain in hand there is no panic; he has always saved money over the years.

examples.zh: 手中有粮，心中不慌，家里多备点米面总不会错。
examples.en: With reserves in hand you feel calm; it can't hurt to keep extra rice and flour at home.

usage.en: Used of savings, stockpiles and skills. Became common again in times of shortages and uncertainty.
usage.zh: 可指存款、储备和本事；物资紧张、局势不明时尤其常见。

pinyin: qíng dài yǔ sǎn, bǎo dài jī liáng
literal: sunny · carry · umbrella, full · carry · hungry · grain
natural: Take an umbrella when it's sunny, take food when you're full

meaning.en: Be prepared in advance for what may come.
meaning.zh: 在条件好的时候就要为困难做准备。

equivalents: Prepare for a rainy day
Better safe than sorry

examples.zh: 晴带雨伞，饱带饥粮，出门多备点吃的。
examples.en: Take an umbrella when it's sunny and food when you're full; bring extra things to eat when you go out.

examples.zh: 爷爷常说晴带雨伞，饱带饥粮，要居安思危。
examples.en: Grandpa often says to take an umbrella in the sunshine and food when full, always thinking of danger in times of peace.

usage.en: Folk advice about forward planning, often said by older people.
usage.zh: 民间的未雨绸缪之言，多出自长辈。

text: 不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门
pinyin: bú zuò kuī xīn shì, bú pà guǐ qiāo mén
variants: 平生不做亏心事，半夜敲门心不惊
literal: not · do · guilty-conscience · deeds, not · fear · ghost · knock · door
natural: If you do nothing to be ashamed of, you needn't fear a ghost's knock

meaning.en: A person with a clear conscience has nothing to fear.
meaning.zh: 只要问心无愧，就不怕别人追究。

equivalents: A clear conscience fears no accusation
Let him who is without sin cast the first stone

examples.zh: 不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门，让他们去查好了。
examples.en: If you do nothing wrong you have nothing to fear, so let them investigate.

examples.zh: 我不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门，随便你们调查。
examples.en: I haven't done anything I'm ashamed of and have nothing to fear, so investigate as you like.

usage.en: Declares innocence. The longer form: 平生不做亏心事，半夜敲门心不惊.
usage.zh: 用来表明自己问心无愧；也说“平生不做亏心事，半夜敲门心不惊”。

pinyin: rén zài zuò, tiān zài kàn
literal: people · are · doing, heaven · is · watching
natural: People act; heaven watches

meaning.en: Whatever people do, Heaven sees it; wrongdoing will not go unpunished.
meaning.zh: 人做的事老天都看得见，做坏事终会有报应。

equivalents: God sees everything
You can't hide from heaven

examples.zh: 人在做，天在看，做坏事早晚要遭报应。
examples.en: People act and heaven watches; sooner or later evil deeds will be punished.

examples.zh: 人在做，天在看，我们做生意要讲良心。
examples.en: What we do is seen by heaven, so we must do business with conscience.

usage.en: A moral warning with a folk-religious flavour; also a call for honesty at work.
usage.zh: 带民间信仰色彩的道德告诫，也用于提醒做事要凭良心。

pinyin: bú shì bú bào, shí hou wèi dào
literal: not · is · not · repay, time · not yet · come
natural: It's not that justice won't come; the time hasn't yet come

meaning.en: Wrongdoers will be punished sooner or later; it is only a matter of time.
meaning.zh: 做了恶事终会受到惩罚，只是时机还没到。

equivalents: The mills of God grind slowly
Justice delayed is not justice denied

examples.zh: 善有善报，恶有恶报，不是不报，时候未到。
examples.en: Good is repaid with good and evil with evil; it's not that it won't come, the time hasn't yet come.

examples.zh: 不是不报，时候未到，他的坏事终会败露。
examples.en: Justice will come eventually; it's just a matter of time before his misdeeds are exposed.

usage.en: Usually quoted in full as 善有善报，恶有恶报，不是不报，时候未到，时辰一到，一切都报.
usage.zh: 常整句引用：“善有善报，恶有恶报，不是不报，时候未到”。
